question.text: Per SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/IMD-I/DF6/P/CIR/2021/584 dated June 25, 2021 referenced in the chapter, the MAXIMUM leverage a Category III AIF can take via derivatives is:

answer.text: 2 times NAV (with investor consent and SEBI disclosure)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter, leverage by a Category III AIF through derivatives or borrowed money should not exceed 2 times the Net Asset Value (NAV) of the Fund, with the prior consent of investors and periodic disclosures/reporting to investors and SEBI. The Trap: 1x understates the regulatory cap; 3x is unauthorised; the 'no leverage' rule applies to Cat I/II AIFs, not Cat III. Note: Three elements travel together for Cat III leverage - the 2x NAV ceiling, prior investor consent, and the periodic disclosure/reporting obligation to investors and SEBI.
